originalPrompt: Research Tailscale, ZeroTier, Nebula and a manually managed WireGuard network for a fleet of 50 Windows, Linux and macOS devices. Compare identity management, NAT traversal, revocation, maintenance burden, pricing and known operational issues. Use current primary sources and distinguish self-hosted from hosted components.
tailscaleAnswer: - **Tailscale:** Personal free (≤3 users per current plan table; page shows $0 up to a small user count); **Standard $8/user/mo**, **Premium $18/user/mo**, Enterprise custom. Devices per user are unlimited on every plan; 50 tagged resources (exit nodes, subnet routers) included, then $1/mo each. For a 50-seat team: ~$400/mo (Standard) or ~$900/mo (Premium). [1]
zerotierAnswer: - **ZeroTier:** Identity is a cryptographically addressed node (public key = its 40-bit ZeroTier address). Membership is authorized by a controller (hosted in ZeroTier Central, or **self-hostable** — the controller is a feature of ZeroTier One). There's no native IdP/SSO integration for end devices; authorization is per-node, managed in the web UI or API. [6] [23]
